description: Opens an HTTP server on this machine through which an outside program can read and change the patch: list, add, move and delete modules, patch and unpatch cables, set any knob and read voltages

params.text: Starts the server on the first press; there is nothing on the panel that stops it again, and a second press does nothing while it is running

inputs.text: Takes the left channel of a signal to be measured; the voltage here is written into a buffer that the server's audio endpoints read, and it goes nowhere else
Takes the right channel of a signal to be measured; the voltage here is written into a buffer that the server's audio endpoints read, and it goes nowhere else

notes: the module does nothing at all until the Start button is pressed, and on its own it only answers HTTP requests: something has to be at the other end of the connection for anything to happen
the maker's own client is an MCP server and a Claude skill, given out through the Patreon page named in the module's browser entry, and they are not part of this plugin
the orb at the top is red while the server is stopped and green while it is running; it is drawn by the module rather than being a lamp, so it cannot be clicked
the server accepts connections only from 127.0.0.1, this machine itself, so nothing on the network can reach the patch through it
the port is 7777 unless the environment variable NTR_WABOT_PORT is set to another number before Rack is started; the panel prints 7777 whatever the port actually is
setting the environment variable NTR_WABOT_TOKEN before Rack is started makes the server refuse any request that does not carry that same string in an X-Wabot-Token header
the two audio jacks are read whether or not anything is patched to them, and they change nothing in the patch: they exist so that the far end of the connection can measure a signal
the audio endpoints give a spectrum on a twelfth-of-an-octave grid from 20Hz up, and a loudness and stereo reading that needs a few seconds of signal before it will answer
